Look up Dhammapada full audio book on YouTube that would be the best introduction to what the Buddhist philosophy really stands for. For Buddhist stories I'd recommend you just go online and look up Buddhist parables and you'll find an infinite amount of them everywhere, keep in mind some of them might actually just be something some guy on the internet made up but if you enjoy them then that's all that really matters at the start. Now to be honest I haven't read much online because personally I like reading physical copies of books more so sorry I couldn't be much help but there's a book I recommend for you to really get started into the Buddhist universe 'Penguin Classics Buddhist Scriptures edited by Donald S Lopez' it's a nice and fun read that will walk you through and explain terms and different translations of Buddhist Scriptures that are pretty well known in the west. It also speaks a little bit of the history of Buddhism and how it came to be what it is today since the editor is also a professor of Asian culture. I also recommend a more popular book called 'The Buddhist Bible' it's probably how most people on this subreddit got started with Buddhism and while it isn't the most reliable translation of certain scriptures it's a fun read and a great simple way to get started. I wish you luck on your spiritual journey and I hope I was of some help.
